title: SettingsClient.get / ipfsDesktop.agentSettings.get
description: Messages of the SettingsClient.get() method (agent-settings-contract task 1.5). On the Desktop bridge this is the IPC channel ipfsDesktop.agentSettings.get; on HTTP it is GET on the settings route with the admin bearer (mcp-agent-settings-api 1.2). The request carries no payload. The response mirrors the server read shape (../settings-read.schema.json) field for field and, like it, never carries key material: a configured API key is reported only as api_key {set, source}. When no admin principal is configured or agent.settings.enabled is false, the HTTP transport answers 404 and the Desktop bridge reports the route as unavailable through status(); neither state is this document.

GetRequest.description: Empty payload. The channel takes no arguments.

backend.description: The effective agent-loop backend, resolved as flags > overlay > config (ADR-0009 section 7). null means no backend is configured; agent surfaces then answer backend_not_configured and the settings page shows its first-run state (assessment-ui 5.4).

Revision.description: Opaque revision of the effective settings, mirroring the server ETag. Every mutating method (set, setApiKey, clearApiKey) requires the current revision; a stale one is rejected with revision_conflict. On HTTP this is the ETag/If-Match header; on IPC it travels as a body field because the channel has no headers.

set.description: Whether a key is configured. Key material is never returned by any read.

source.description: Where the configured key comes from: settings_api (written through setApiKey, on Desktop held in safeStorage and applied to the sidecar), environment (the variable named by llm.api_key), file (a SecretRef file, for example a Kubernetes Secret mount). Present exactly when set is true.

ApiKeyStatus.description: Key presence and provenance only, mirroring ../settings-read.schema.json. There is no field that can carry key material.

kind.description: openai: an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint (G10). uar: kubo creates and proxies a Universal Agent Runtime agent (D14, ADR-0010).

base_url.description: Base URL of the backend endpoint. Maps from assessment-ui 5.2 openai.baseUrl and uar.url.

model.description: The effective model name. Maps from assessment-ui 5.2 openai.model.

safety_prefix.description: The fixed safety prefix the server always prepends (mcp-agent-hot-reload 1.4). Set by the binary, not writable, cannot be removed, emptied or overridden by custom.

custom.description: The operator-configured part of the system prompt. May be empty. It only ever extends safety_prefix, never replaces it.
